title: Secret resume-phase setter live-breakpoint retry (2026-07-16, r3-final: direct write-site arm + physical-address detection; still rejected, third distinct failure mode)
purpose: Third attempt at the BUILD-QUEUE.md line-358 leaf, per r2's suggested next steps: arm the setter WRITE instruction directly (BP 4465:0561) instead of assuming a dispatch-loop re-entry at offset 0000, and detect the live hit by computed physical address rather than by literal segment text, since DOSBox-X 'BP segment:offset' resolves to a physical/linear-address match in real mode (independently proven mid-session, see below).

change_summary_over_r2: Arm 'BP {resumeParserSegment}:{runtimeSetterWriteOffset}' (4465:0561, the write instruction itself, byte-confirmed present in prior post-hoc RAM scans) directly, in the same arm-before-RUN + BPLIST-readback-confirmed-stopped discipline r2 proved correct -- no longer arming the unverified dispatch-loop head at offset 0000.

Replaced the r2 detection regex (which required the literal text 'CS=4465\s+EIP=00000561') with a physical-address comparison: every poll parses whatever CS:EIP the live snapshot actually reports, computes ((CS<<4)+EIP) & 0xFFFFF, and compares it to the precomputed target physical address (0x44BB1). This was required because an earlier same-day run (superseded, not separately filed) proved live that the CPU can and does report a *different* segment:offset alias (CS=43C9 EIP=00000F21) whose physical address is bit-for-bit identical to 4465:0561 -- (0x43C9<<4)+0xF21 == (0x4465<<4)+0x0561 == 0x44BB1 exactly -- and that 43C9:0EC7 (the matching prologue address under that alias) exactly matches GAME.OVR's own file-relative vm_SetMemoryValue offset (+0xEC7 from overlay 9's base), independently corroborating that alias as plausible.

Added a Get-Sha256Hex helper (pure .NET SHA256, no Get-FileHash cmdlet dependency) to remove an unrelated environment fragility (Get-FileHash was found unavailable under this shell's powershell.exe host due to a $env:PSModulePath ordering/module-shadowing issue -- orthogonal to the resume-setter hypothesis, fixed so it stops being a confound).

run.post_run_process_check: Get-Process -Name dosbox-x returned no results after the run (verified explicitly); Get-Process -Name python returned only two unrelated pre-existing processes from 2026-07-06 and 2026-07-15, not this run's own ollama-auto-combat agent -- confirming that agent process was also cleanly stopped by the script's own cleanup path before the finally block ran.

stage_save_unchanged.note: identical to the r1/r2 stage hash; the hash-locked stage directory is still reusable and was not mutated by this run

arm_before_run_proof.claim: The write-site breakpoint (4465:0561) was armed and BPLIST-confirmed while the debugger was genuinely stopped (CS=407F EIP=00000000, the operand-parser hit), before the cursor loop's first RUN -- same discipline r2 proved correct, now applied to the write site instead of the dispatch-loop head.
arm_before_run_proof.note: 'I-> _' is the debugger's own command prompt, present only when genuinely stopped -- not '(Running)'. This is the same evidentiary bar r2 established.

physical_address_matching_worked_as_desi.claim: This part of the hypothesis is now proven, not inferred: a live poll snapshot DID report a hit at a segment:offset alias other than the literal arm-time text, and the physical-address comparison correctly recognized it as a match, where a literal-text comparison (as used by r2 and by an earlier same-day superseded attempt) would have missed it.
physical_address_matching_worked_as_desi.observed_live_registers: CS=442D EIP=000008E1 (build/dosbox-x-secret-combat-resume-setter-20260716-r3-final/outcome-area-setter-poll-console.txt), genuinely stopped (console ends in the 'I-> _' prompt, not '(Running)')
physical_address_matching_worked_as_desi.physical_address_check: (0x442D << 4) + 0x08E1 = 0x442D0 + 0x8E1 = 0x44BB1, exactly equal to the precomputed target ((0x4465 << 4) + 0x0561 = 0x44BB1). The detection loop's physical-address match fired correctly.

new_failure_mode.observed: The live disassembly at the reported CS:IP (442D:000008E1) is 'mov al,[bp-0D]' / 'push ax' / 'mov al,[bp-0F]' / 'push ax' / 'mov al,[bp+06]' / 'push ax' / 'push cs' / 'call 00000697' -- an entirely different instruction sequence, not the expected Area1 setter write ('mov word ptr es:[di+0x6A00],dx', bytes 26 89 95 00 6A).

byte_validation.verdict: neither the prologue nor the write bytes match at the target physical address; the harness's own byte-validation guard correctly rejected this as a false positive and threw rather than reporting a fabricated success

new_failure_mode.distinguishing_fact: This is a genuinely new and more specific failure mode than r1 (breakpoint-registration timing bug) or r2 (breakpoint proven armed and never removed, but CS:IP never observed at the assumed offset-0000 entry at all). Here the breakpoint DID fire, at the correct physical address, while the debugger was genuinely stopped -- but the code resident at that physical address at the moment of the hit is not the Area1 setter function. The most likely explanation (inferred, not proven): DOSBox-X's physical/linear-address breakpoint mechanism is inherently vulnerable to this under Gold Box's VROOMM overlay system, because VROOMM reuses fixed physical paragraph ranges for different overlay payloads at different points during execution. The setter function's byte-identical image was independently confirmed resident at this physical address by post-hoc RAM scans taken earlier in the same general timeframe (map_secret_runtime_setter.py, and this session's own operand-parser-phase evidence), but by the time combat outcome processing actually revisited this physical page live, VROOMM had already swapped a different overlay's code into it. A breakpoint keyed to a physical address derived from an earlier snapshot therefore cannot reliably distinguish 'the setter is executing here again' from 'some unrelated later overlay happens to occupy the same physical bytes now' -- both trigger an identical DOSBox-X BP hit.
new_failure_mode.combat_victory_injection_applied: Yes -- combat-victory-injection.json shows the bounded foe-count/hydra-HP injection and the six D,Q party-turn-completion keypresses were sent before this false-positive hit occurred, consistent with r1/r2's InjectCombatVictory path; the debugger was already free-running into 2D tactical combat at the point of injection (same 'debugger already free-running into combat' log line r2 established as expected, not an error).
new_failure_mode.natural_route_completion_not_recaptured_: Because the harness's own byte-validation guard threw immediately on detecting the false-positive hit (by design -- 'do not force a false positive to avoid a third no'), the script's finally block terminated the DOSBox-X process before the bounded auto-combat timeout path could run and capture a final post-hoc RAM snapshot. This run therefore does NOT independently re-confirm the natural-route completion (cursor 0x82C6, friends/foes 6/0, consumed word 0->4 at physical 0x5515A) that r1, r2, and the original 2026-07-15 natural run each captured. That three-times-independently-reproduced fact is not called into question by this gap -- it simply was not re-observed in this specific run because the run was deliberately stopped early rather than allowed to mask the false positive.

revised_root_cause_hypothesis.claim_boundary: hypothesis only, not proven this session -- offered to focus any future attempt
revised_root_cause_hypothesis.text: Both suggested r2 next-steps (arm the write site directly; or single-step forward from a last-confirmed-live breakpoint) share an unstated assumption: that whichever physical/segment location last showed the setter's byte-identical image is the one the CPU will revisit during the real resume call, if any. This run shows that assumption is false in general for a VROOMM-managed overlay arena -- the physical page's occupant changes over time, so a breakpoint (which DOSBox-X resolves physically) armed against a stale snapshot's address can and does collide with unrelated later code. A reliable live capture of the actual resume-phase setter write, if it is reachable via any surviving overlay copy at all, likely requires either (a) re-verifying the target physical address's bytes immediately before relying on a hit (this run's own byte-validation guard already does this, and correctly rejected the false positive -- so the guard is doing its job; the gap is that no armed candidate address has yet coincided with a genuine, byte-matching, live hit), or (b) the single-stepping approach r2 also suggested: stepping instruction-by-instruction forward from a known-good, always-resident breakpoint (e.g. the tactical-phase 41B7:0000 or the combat-continue Enter prompt) through the entire resume transition, logging every CS:IP, so the actual live call path is observed directly rather than inferred from any prior snapshot's address -- at the cost of a very large step budget through 2D tactical combat, which this project's harness does not currently support (2D tactical combat itself has no ECL breakpoint to gate single-stepping, and step-counts through real-time tactical AI/combat resolution could be in the tens of thousands to millions of instructions).
revised_root_cause_hypothesis.not_yet_falsified: It remains unproven either way whether the Area1 setter write for this specific resume path is ever executed live at all during natural gameplay (as opposed to the byte-identical function existing in RAM without necessarily being called via this particular ECL opcode path) -- three independent runs' post-hoc final-RAM evidence (consumed word 0->4, cursor 0x82C6/0x82C5) is consistent with it being called, but does not by itself prove which physical/segment address performed the write, since the SetMemoryValue-equivalent logic could plausibly be reached through more than one relocatable copy across the VROOMM arena.

suggested_next_attempt: Do not reuse a single fixed physical address computed from an earlier snapshot as the sole arm target for the entire run. Instead, immediately before relying on any hit, re-derive the candidate address (or re-verify its bytes) as close as possible to the actual moment of interest, or arm on multiple candidate physical pages simultaneously and byte-validate each hit independently (as this run's own guard already does per-hit) until a genuine byte match is found or the run times out.

Pursue the single-step-from-known-good-checkpoint approach explicitly, accepting the step-budget cost: start single-stepping (F11, not RUN) from the last confirmed-live checkpoint before tactical combat resolution (e.g. right after the injected-victory party-turn-completion keypresses), logging CS:IP on every step to a rolling buffer, and stop either on a byte-exact match to the setter's prologue/write bytes at the CURRENT CS:IP (not a precomputed physical address) or on a step-budget/timeout. This directly observes the true call path without assuming any address in advance.

Alternatively, treat the resume-phase setter capture as a separate, narrower research question from the BUILD-QUEUE.md leaf's original two-stage design, and consider whether the leaf's acceptance criteria (validate a specific reached CS:0561, in a specific segment) can be relaxed to 'validate the write occurs via A byte-exact 26 89 95 00 6A instruction at whatever live CS:IP is genuinely observed, with correct ES/EDI/EDX preconditions' -- which is what this run's detection logic already does correctly; the remaining gap is finding an armed address that is actually revisited with byte-identical code, not the detection or validation logic itself.
checkbox_status: BUILD-QUEUE.md line ~358 remains unchecked; this is a third rejected attempt, with a new and more specific failure mode than r1 or r2: the physical-address detection approach worked exactly as designed (a live hit was correctly recognized despite a different segment:offset alias, and the byte-validation guard correctly rejected it as a false positive), but the specific physical address armed for this run was, at the moment of the hit, occupied by unrelated overlay code rather than the Area1 setter -- most likely because Gold Box's VROOMM overlay manager had reused that physical paragraph range for a different payload by the time tactical-combat resolution revisited it live.
